restaurants.note: A minute up the lane from the noodle house; last order 16:00. ⚑ From October to May it runs a food menu and not only sweets, so in November it is a lunch — four dishes, ¥1,300 to ¥2,200. ⚠ Its closing days are irregular and announced only on its own Instagram, so an open day cannot be assumed.

restaurants.note: About fifty metres from Suzuriishi-tei and at much the same height on the steps, so the two are one stop rather than two. ⚠ Its closing days are irregular, and the rule that clears today — no closures from October to early December — is second-hand; the shop publishes nothing itself. ⚑ Two options behind it cannot fail the same way. It also closes on irregular days that it publishes nowhere readable.

This is the honten, at Higashi-Shiokōji Mukaihata-chō 845.

restaurants.note: Sixty-three seats, tables and tatami, which is what makes it walk-in-safe on a peak autumn day; no table can be booked here in any case. ⚠ Its two channels name two different card brands and neither names Visa or Mastercard, so carry cash for it. ⚑ Lunch here is not optional — the mountain eateries close around 16:00 to 17:00, so this is the day's only meal on the ridge. Dinner is back in Kyoto.

Thirty seconds along the frontage from the one above, so checking it costs nothing — the bigger room of the two, and it takes cards. ⚠ Its closing days are irregular on both channels and neither publishes a policy, so do not assume an open day. ⚑ If every seat in the village is taken on a peak Thursday: kakinoha-zushi is leaf-wrapped, room-temperature food made to be carried, sold over the counter at Yakko, Tatsumi (たつみ) and Daiyo (醍予) — buy a box and eat it at the Hanayagura viewpoint on the way up. ⚑ One named stop that is not lunch: Nakai Shunpū-dō (中井春風堂), in front of the Zaō-dō — kuzumochi and kuzukiri ¥900 each, made to order in about twenty minutes and eaten within ten. On the second basement level at Kyoto Station's east exit — 136 m, no street and no weather, on the night the day is most likely to arrive late and tired. ⚠ Two of its three channels print 07:00 to 22:00 with last order 21:30 and the third prints a wider 06:00 to 23:00 on weekdays. Work to the narrower pair; it is the one two channels agree on.

meals.time_hint: On Omotesandō, 15:00–16:15 — after the Misen descent at 14:45, with the dusk foreshore walk after it

restaurants.note: ⚡ It serves both of the day's dishes under one roof — grilled oysters, and anago-meshi at ¥2,900 with grilled eel at ¥2,700 and anago-musubi at ¥1,200 for two, alongside udon, soba, tonkatsu and fried-prawn sets — so on a day with 535 metres of stone stairs in it there is no second stop. Thirty seconds along the street from the primary and taking orders until six — ninety minutes later — which is what makes it survive a badly delayed descent. Grilled oysters from the front of the shop; budget ¥750 for a pair, the higher of two published figures. ⚠ It cannot be confirmed open in advance and may shut early once the day's oysters are gone. ⚑ The name is 牡蠣屋 — a search for かき屋 will not find it. ✅ If both counters have shut behind you, two things still work with no detour: Momijidō Honten (紅葉堂 本店) on the shopping street to 17:30, fried momiji-manjū ¥190, ⛔ cash only, five minutes; and Anagomeshi Ueno (あなごめし うえの) two minutes from the mainland ferry terminal, last order 18:30 — off the 17:25 ferry you land at 17:35 with an hour left. It would collide with dinner, so it is the safety net, not the plan.

restaurants.note: Ten minutes on foot from Hiroshima Station's north exit. ⚡ The 23:00 close is the useful fact tonight: at the end of the trip's hardest day, on a return leg that is a ladder of ferries and trains, it clears what the night needs by two and a half hours — the 17:55 ferry, the 18:03 train and the 18:19 train all cost you nothing. ⛔ Cash and PayPay only, and tonight's backup takes no credit cards either. ⚑ This does put okonomiyaki at Saturday lunch and Sunday dinner; if you want it once only, yesterday's swap does it in a single move.

⚡ The zero-walk answer after 535 metres of stone stairs: you step off the JR train and are at the counter without leaving the building — 56 metres, ekie's first floor. ⚠ It prints no closing day of its own and keeps the ekie building's calendar, which is not published far enough ahead to read; tonight's primary is outside the building.

meals.time_hint: Bought at ekie between about 11:30 and 12:30, eaten on the 12:43 Nozomi

restaurants.note: ekie's 2nd floor, in the おみやげ館 souvenir hall — that is the sign to look for. About ¥2,430 for the regular size — a reported figure, not the shop's own. ⚠ It prints no closing day of its own and keeps the ekie building's calendar.

restaurants.cuisine: Ekiben — six counters inside the Shinkansen gates
restaurants.note: ⛔ Skip Musashi (むさし 広島駅新幹線弁当工房) — the best-known bento name at this station closes every Monday and this is a Monday. Every one of the others is open and one is on your own platform, so the ekiben cannot fail — only the specific box can. Hiroshima Ekiben (廣島驛辨當) in the Meihinkan zone, 5:30 to 21:30; a second Hiroshima Ekiben counter on the Tokyo-direction platform, 8:00 to 20:00; and the Seven-Eleven Kiosk on that same platform, 5:35 to 22:00. ⚑ Two more are one stop, not three: Kyō no Sushi (鮨処 京の寿し) and Ajiroya (あじろや), both 8:00 to 20:00, are counters inside Omiyage Kaidō (おみやげ街道) at the central Shinkansen gate, itself open 6:00 to 22:00 with an ATM. ⚑ The label to look for on the sign is 銘品館.

meals.time_hint: At the hotel by about 16:55 with nothing after it — 17:30 to 19:00, your choice

restaurants.note: Ten minutes on foot from the hotel, inside the home district, three minutes from Awajichō. It opens at 17:30 and last-orders at 20:00 — twenty minutes before the close — while you are back at the hotel about 16:55 with nothing after it. ⚠ The shop asks you to check its own social account for the days it trades, so an open day cannot be assumed; it also stops when the noodles run out.

About 150 metres from the hotel, on the first floor of Atre Akihabara 1 — on the walk home from the Shinkansen arrival, so no transfer and no separate leg. Last order 22:00; cards and IC, no reservations. ⚡ That puts two hours behind the primary's 20:00 last order, so if the Shinkansen slips or the November calendar closes the primary, the night still eats 150 metres from the bed. ⚠ Neither of its own channels states a closing day, so it follows Atre's calendar.

meals.time_hint: In Ryōgoku, about 12:30 — between the station and the Edo-Tokyo Museum

restaurants.note: One minute from Ryōgoku's JR east exit, 103 metres, on the 2nd and 3rd floors; the lunch service runs 11:00 to 15:00. ⚠ It is bookable online as well as walk-in, so it can be full — and what answers that is the room itself: a hundred and twenty seats across tables, tatami and sunken hearths, at half past twelve on an ordinary Tuesday. ⚑ A third name if both of the first two fail: Sumo Chaya Terao (相撲茶屋 寺尾), 173 metres — run by a former wrestler who is the elder brother of the Terao it is named for, not by Terao himself. ⚠ Unlike the other two, nothing about this one was checked — not its seats, not its closing day, not its hours. It is a name to walk to, not a verified fallback.

42 metres from Ryōgoku's west exit and on the same block as the Edo-Tokyo Museum — it sits literally between the station and the museum. Lunch last order is 14:00, an hour before the close, and it seats 88 at tables — so like the primary, this one answers a busy day with the size of the room rather than with a wait. ⚠ The only closing rule either channel publishes is a summer one, so treat November as unknown. 🔴 Do not confuse it with the other branch: Kirishima's honten, 97 metres away, is closed Mondays and Tuesdays, so it is dead on this date. Two branches of one name with different closing days.

meals.time_hint: Back at Ryōgoku about 17:15, or about 18:00 if the Kiyosumi garden coda is taken — a table around 17:45–18:15

restaurants.note: On Yokozuna Yokochō, off Ryōgoku's east exit. Last order 22:00, which makes the Kiyosumi detour free: back at Ryōgoku about 18:00 with it, about 17:15 without, and neither competes with dinner. ✅ Open all year bar a new-year closure, with no irregular closing days. ⚑ The upside option: Teuchi Ren (手打式 らぁ麺 蓮), eight minutes on foot and six from Morishita, so it sits on the Kiyosumi axis, 17:00 to 22:00, closed Mondays. 🔴 Take it only if there is no line: seven seats, cash only, and waiting inside is not permitted. On the last night, with no following day to absorb a failed walk-in, that is a bet and not a fallback. ⚑ The kanji is 蓮, not 練 — the wrong character will not find it on the ground.

At Akihabara, two Sōbu stops from Ryōgoku and about four minutes — and 150 metres from the hotel, so it is also the answer if you simply ride straight home. ⚑ But check the clock before you ride: its evening service does not open until 18:00, so on the early version of this day — back at Ryōgoku about 17:15, at Akihabara by about 17:25 — you would be standing outside it. Either take the Kiyosumi garden coda and arrive after six, or eat at the primary in Ryōgoku, which is already serving.
